The Brief SpaceX sent 29 Starlink satellites into low Earth orbit during an early morning launch on Tuesday.A Falcon 9 rocket carrying the satellites launched around 5:33 a.m. EDT from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station.The Starlink constellation is made up of thousands of satellites. CLICK TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX LOCAL APP The satellites were on board a Falcon 9 rocket, which blasted off around 5:33 a.m. EDT from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The first stage booster completed its 26th flight and its 19th Starlink mission. It successfully landed on the droneship "Just Read the Instructions," which was positioned in the Atlantic Ocean.
